tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Harnack convergence theorem]1. ch2:2.9\group chapter-2 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0034 ↗ gt.thm2.5 ↗ gt.thm2.8 Let $u_j$ increase monotonically through harmonic functions on $\Omega $. If $u_j(y)$ is bounded at one point, then $u_j$ converges uniformly on every bounded $\Omega '\Subset \Omega $ to a harmonic function.
Proof

↗ gt.thm2.5 ↗ gt.thm2.8 ↗ gt.thm2.9 \sketch Apply Harnack’s inequality to the nonnegative harmonic differences $u_m-u_j$. Their values at $y$ are Cauchy, hence the differences tend uniformly to zero on compact subdomains. Theorem 30 identifies the limit as harmonic.

□
